AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND CONTEXT
AbstractText.content: Cervical transforaminal epidural steroid injection (TFESI) is considered one of the most effective treatments for radicular pain induced by cervical foraminal stenosis.

AbstractText.Label: PURPOSE
AbstractText.content: To evaluate the treatment outcome of TFESI according to the severity of cervical foraminal stenosis DESIGN: Retrospective study.

AbstractText.Label: PATIENT SAMPLE
AbstractText.content: Fifty-three patients with cervical radiculopathy due to cervical foraminal stenosis.

AbstractText.Label: OUTCOME MEASURES
AbstractText.content: Pain intensity was evaluated using a numeric rating scale (NRS) at pretreatment, 2 weeks, and 1, 2, and 3 months after TFESI.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Patients were divided into two groups according to the severity of stenosis by cervical axial MRI findings. Twenty-two patients were assigned to group A (non-severe stenosis) and 31 patients were assigned to group B (severe stenosis).

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Thirty-seven (69.8%) of 53 patients showed successful treatment outcome (more than 50% reduction in the NRS score at 3 months). The patients in both groups showed a significant decrease in NRS scores at 2 weeks and at 1, 2, and 3 months after TFESI. However, the effect of TFESI was not significantly different between patients with non-severe cervical foraminal stenosis and those with severe cervical foraminal stenosis.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: The treatment outcome of cervical TFESI did not different according to the severity of cervical foraminal stenosis. However, based on our results, we suggest that TFESI can be a beneficial clinical option for managing the radicular pain due to cervical foraminal stenosis.
